record.paper_title: The Strong Convergence of Subgradients of Convex Functions Along Directions: Perspectives and Open Problems
record.original_question: Let Q be a subset of a Hilbert space H such that every point of H has a unique farthest point in Q. Must Q be a singleton? The paper presents this as V. Klee's still-open farthest-point problem and explains that a sufficiently strong positive result on directional convergence of subgradients would resolve it.

evidence.quote: A good example, where the directional convergence of subgradients would work effectively, is the problem by V . Klee— it is still open ; see [4]—suppose Q is a subset of Hilbert space H such that each point of H admits a unique farthest point in Q . Must Q consist of a single point?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $H$ be a (real) Hilbert space and let $Q \subseteq H$ be a nonempty subset with the property that for every $x \in H$ the farthest-point map
$$F_Q(x) = \{q \in Q : \|x - q\| = \sup_{q' \in Q} \|x - q'\|\}$$
is a singleton (i.e., every point of $H$ admits a unique farthest point in $Q$). Must $Q$ itself consist of a single point?
artifact.status_search_result: Klee's uniquely-remotal (farthest point) problem is well known to remain open in infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces. Klee (1961) settled the finite-dimensional Euclidean case, but the Hilbert-space version is widely cited as a long-standing open conjecture in recent surveys and problem collections on nonlinear analysis and optimization.

status_evidence.title: Potpourri of Conjectures and Open Questions in Nonlinear Analysis and Optimization
status_evidence.snippet: Lists the uniquely remotal/farthest point conjecture as a long-standing open problem.
status_evidence.claim: The uniquely remotal set conjecture in Hilbert/Banach space is listed as open.

status_evidence.title: Bregman distances and Klee sets
status_evidence.snippet: Klee (1960) proved finite-dimensional case; infinite-dimensional case open.
status_evidence.claim: Hilbert space version of Klee's problem unresolved.
